items.title: 2.10 Ek dimension mein inelastic takrao (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 2.10 with Fig. 2.16 and Example 2.10 (PDF 45-46, 50; printed 42-43, 47).

blocks.text: Do jism lein jin ke mass m₁ aur m₂ hain aur jo ek hi lakeer mein v⃗₁i aur v⃗₂i velocities se chal rahe hain, aur v⃗₁i > v⃗₂i (peechhe wala tez hai). Is soorat mein m₁ ko projectile aur m₂ ko target kehte hain. Kuch der (t) baad dono inelastic takrao karte hain aur aapas mein chipak jate hain. Ab un ka mila hua mass m₁ + m₂ hai jo takrao ke baad final velocity v⃗f se chalta hai (Fig. 2.16).

blocks.alt: Takrao se pehle: gend m1 velocity v1i se aur bari gend m2 velocity v2i se, dono daen taraf. Takrao ke baad: ek bara jism m1 + m2, andar gehra hissa, velocity vf se daen taraf.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.16: Ek dimension mein perfectly inelastic takrao (kitab ki Figure 2.16 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: Takrao perfectly inelastic hai, phir bhi kul momentum barqarar rehta hai. Momentum conservation ke qanoon se:

blocks.latex: \text{Total momentum of system before collision} = \text{Total momentum of the system after collision}
blocks.text_alt: Total momentum of system before collision = Total momentum of the system after collision

blocks.text: Yeh takrao ke baad mile hue jism ki mushtarka (common) velocity hai.

Yani m₁ ki velocity mass ratio m₁/(m₁ + m₂) ke hisaab se kam ho jati hai. m₁ ka mass jitna zyada ho, mila hua jism utna tez chalta hai.

Inelastic takrao mein kinetic energy ka jo hissa (fraction) zaya hota hai:
Eq. (2.37) se vf ki qeemat rakhein:

blocks.text_alt: ((K.E)i - (K.E)f)/(K.E)i = ([½m₁v₁i² + ½m₂v₂i²] - ½(m₁ + m₂)[m₁/(m₁ + m₂)]² v₁i²) / [½m₁v₁i² + ½m₂v₂i²]

blocks.text: Ab khaas soorat lein jab target m₂ ruka hua ho (v₂i = 0). Hal karne se:

Yeh inelastic takrao mein zaya hone wali kinetic energy ka hissa hai. Is se saaf hai ke ek dimension ke inelastic takrao mein energy zaya hoti hai. Misal: m₁ = m₂ ho to aadhi kinetic energy zaya ho jati hai.

blocks.title: Example 2.10
blocks.problem: 2 kg mass ki projectile 4 m s⁻¹ ki initial velocity se daen taraf chal kar 3 kg ke ruke hue target se takrati hai. Takrao ke baad dono chipak kar ek jism ki tarah 1.6 m s⁻¹ se chalte hain. Momentum ka conservation aur energy ka nuqsan dikhayein. (Kitab mein yeh example topic 2.12 ke baad chhapa hai.)
steps: Pehle ka momentum (x-simt): pₓ = m₁v₁ₓ + m₂v₂ₓ = (2 kg × 4 m s⁻¹) + (3 kg × 0) = 8 kg m s⁻¹
Mila hua mass M = 2 kg + 3 kg = 5 kg, final velocity 1.6 m s⁻¹
Baad ka momentum: M vf = 5 kg × 1.6 m s⁻¹ = 8 kg m s⁻¹, yani momentum barqarar hai
Pehle ki K.E. = ½ × 2 kg × (4 m s⁻¹)² + ½ × 3 kg × 0 = 16 J
Baad ki K.E. = ½ × 5 kg × (1.6 m s⁻¹)² = 6.4 J
Energy ka nuqsan = 16 J - 6.4 J = 9.6 J
blocks.answer: Momentum barqarar hai lekin 9.6 J kinetic energy zaya hui. Yeh ek dimension ka perfectly inelastic takrao hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab is example ko "perfectly inelastic collision in 2D" kehti hai. Lekin dono jism takrao se pehle aur baad ek hi seedhi lakeer (x-simt) mein chalte hain, is liye yeh ek dimension (1D) ka takrao hai, 2D ka nahi.

blocks.caption: Perfectly inelastic seedha takrao
rows: vf = 1.6 m s⁻¹; K.E. 16 J se 6.4 J, yani 9.6 J zaya (3/5 = 60%)

blocks.prompt: Example 2.10 ke jawab equations (2.37) aur (2.38) se check karein.
blocks.explanation: vf = m₁v₁i/(m₁ + m₂) = 2 × 4/5 = 1.6 m s⁻¹, jaisa diya gaya hai. Zaya hissa m₂/(m₁ + m₂) = 3/5 = 0.6 hona chahiye, aur waqai 9.6 J / 16 J = 0.6.

items: Perfectly inelastic: jism chipak jate hain; momentum barqarar: m₁v₁i + m₂v₂i = (m₁ + m₂)vf; target ruka hua ho to vf = m₁v₁i/(m₁ + m₂) aur zaya K.E. ka hissa m₂/(m₁ + m₂). Example 2.10: momentum pehle aur baad 8 kg m s⁻¹, 16 J mein se 9.6 J zaya.
